newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa JSE turnover up 50.4 pct to end-Feb 1997.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa JSE turnover up 50.4 pct to end-Feb 1997.

text.p: Turnover on South Africa's Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE), excluding arbitrage deals, surged 50.4 percent in the months of January and February compared to the same period last year.
The JSE said in a statement trade worth worth 28.83 billion rand has been concluded since the start of the year until February 28, compared with 19.17 billion rand in the same period in 1995.
It said its market capitalisation had risen by 7.5 percent in the first two months of this year and stood at 1,215 billion rand on February 28. On that date last year it stood at 1,099 billion rand.

In U.S. dollar terms the JSE's market capitalisation was worth $248.21 billion on January 31, 1997 compared with $241.57 billion at the end of 1996 -- keeping it at position 16 in the world stock exchange league.
The bourse slipped four notches in this ranking in 1996 from 12th place in 1995, reflecting a dismal performance by the market in dollar terms.

However, ranked by dollar turnover, the JSE, at end January 1997 fell to 32nd position among the 45 member stock exhanges of the Federation Internationale des Bourses de Valeurs from 29th position at the end of 1996.
Its poor liquidity ratio also saw it slide even further to position 39 from 38 at year end last year on that yardstick.

The JSE said net foreign purchases on the bourse stood at 1.92 billion rand in the first two months of 1997. Net foreign buys of shares for the whole of 1996 stood at 5.25 billion rand and 4.81 billion rand in 1995.
For the month ended February 1997, liquidity improved to 17.1 percent from 10.3 percent in February last year, reflecting an increase of 66 percent.
